title: Reading `git status`
reading_goal: Read the explanation of the output from the `git status` command to check the current Git working status.
code:
git status

On branch main
Your branch is up to date with origin/main.

nothing to commit, working tree clean
question: What does "working tree clean" mean?
choices: All the files have been deleted.
There are no changes to commit
answer: There are no changes to commit
explanation: Working tree clean means Git sees no tracked changes or ordinary untracked files to commit. Ignored files may still exist, and 'up to date with origin/main' compares against the locally stored remote-tracking ref from the latest fetch; it does not prove the server's live state.
project_context: That's why we check `git status clean` at the end of each extension task.

title: Reading "untracked" and "unstaged"
reading_goal: It distinguishes between files that Git does not yet track and files that have been modified but not added.
code:
Changes not staged for commit:
  modified: src/pwa/app.js

Untracked files:
  data/lessons/new_lesson.json
question: What is the status of the files in "Untracked files"?
choices: Files that have already been committed
New files that Git does not yet track
answer: New files that Git does not yet track
explanation: The newly created lesson JSON file may appear as "untracked" until you run `git add`. "Untracked" refers to new files that Git is not yet tracking, while "unstaged" refers to changes that have been made but not added to a commit. You must distinguish between the two when running `git status`.
project_context: It is normal for new v33 lesson files to initially appear as "untracked."

title: Reading "git add"
reading_goal: Understand the command used to add files to the staging area for inclusion in a commit.
question: What is the role of `git add` in the basic Git workflow?
choices: Prepare the changes to be included in the next commit
answer: Prepare the changes to be included in the next commit
explanation: The `git add` command moves modified files to the staging area, preparing them to be included in the next commit. This is a step in preparing for a commit, not the step of pushing to a remote repository. Since not all modified files are automatically committed, you should check their staged status using `git status`.
project_context: To commit both the lesson JSON and app.js, you must add both of them.

title: Reading Git Commits
reading_goal: Understand what a commit is—it records staged changes as a single entry.
code: git commit -m "Add Git workflow reading cards"
question: What is the purpose of a commit message?
choices: Briefly record the purpose of this change
answer: Briefly record the purpose of this change
explanation: The `git commit` command saves prepared changes as a single entry. The commit message tells you what you did when you review the change history later. A good commit message briefly notes the reason for and scope of the changes, allowing you to reconstruct the flow of events later just by looking at the log. Therefore, the correct answer is “Briefly record the purpose of this change.”
project_context: If you include topic-specific extensions in your commit messages, as in v28–v32, it makes them easier to track.

title: Reading "git push"
reading_goal: Understand the command for pushing a local commit to a GitHub remote repository.
code:
git push

To https://github.com/user/repo.git
   abc1234..def5678  main -> main
question: What does main -> main mean here?
choices: The main file has been deleted.
The commit from the local main branch has been pushed to the remote main branch.
answer: The commit from the local main branch has been pushed to the remote main branch.
explanation: This output says commits after abc1234 on local main updated the named remote's main ref to def5678. A successful push proves the repository update, not a successful GitHub Pages deployment. Check the separately configured build and deployment status as well.
project_context: If the static site is configured to deploy from main, a separate deployment may start after the push.

title: Reading `git log`
reading_goal: Check the commit history and read the latest commit hash.
code:
git log --oneline -5

0998190 Add files paths and project structure reading cards
4d2080b Fix v31 dict object card answer
question: What is 0998190?
choices: A short hash that points to a commit
answer: A short hash that points to a commit
explanation: git log --oneline shows each commit with an abbreviated hash and subject. 0998190 is a prefix of the full object ID and identifies a commit when that prefix is sufficiently unique in the repository. If it is ambiguous, use the longer hash Git requests or the full hash.
project_context: If a problem arises, you can trace back to the commit where things started going wrong.

title: Reading `git diff`
reading_goal: Understand how to use `diff` to check which lines have changed before committing.
question: Why do you check `git diff` before committing?
choices: To set up automatic deployment to GitHub
To check for any unintended changes
answer: To check for any unintended changes
explanation: In this form, git diff compares app.js in the working tree with the index, so it mainly shows changes that have not been staged. Changes already staged by git add require git diff --cached. Review both kinds of diff before committing.
project_context: This is useful for checking whether `lessonFiles` in `app.js` has been preserved.

title: Read "git restore" carefully
reading_goal: Understand the risks of using `restore` to revert uncommitted changes.
question: What are the risks of this command?
choices: Uncommitted changes in app.js may be lost
All browser cache will be cleared
answer: Uncommitted changes in app.js may be lost
explanation: By default, git restore <file> replaces the working-tree file with the index version, so unstaged edits can be lost while staged changes remain. Check status and both diffs first, and distinguish --source or --staged when restoring from HEAD or changing the staged state.
project_context: This is used when a patch goes wrong, but you have to be careful not to lose the changes you actually need.

title: branch: Basic Reading
reading_goal: Understand the difference between the "main" branch and the "work" branch.
question: What does this command mean?
choices: Create a new work branch and switch to it
answer: Create a new work branch and switch to it
explanation: A branch is a Git feature that creates a separate workflow from the main branch. It allows you to safely carry out experimental work or make major changes and then merge them later. Changes that you’re hesitant to apply directly to the main branch are tested on a new branch and then merged. Therefore, the correct answer is “Create a new branch and switch to it.”
project_context: Testing a large change on a work branch before merging it into main helps keep main stable.

title: An Introduction to Merge Conflicts
reading_goal: Understand the conflict indicators that appear when the same line is edited differently by different users.
question: What does this sign mean?
choices: Git was unable to automatically determine which change to select
answer: Git was unable to automatically determine which change to select
explanation: <<<<<<<, =======, and >>>>>>> mark the two conflicting versions. Git could not decide which content to retain, so a person must create the correct final value, remove every marker, test it, and then add and commit the resolution. The marked block itself is not valid Python.
project_context: This can happen when multiple patches modify the same line in a file like app.js.

title: Read About the GitHub Pages Deployment Workflow
reading_goal: Understand the basic workflow for deploying a static app to GitHub Pages.
code:
local change
git add
git commit
git push
configured Pages build/deploy
public URL updated
question: What steps are usually required first for changes to be reflected in a GitHub Pages URL?
explanation: A local change must first reach the remote repository through commit and push. Pages then starts a build and deployment only if that branch and folder, or an Actions workflow, is configured as its source. A successful push alone does not guarantee that the public URL was updated, so check deployment status and the deployed revision.
project_context: Changes that are visible only locally will not be reflected in Pages until they are pushed.

title: Reading the CRLF Warning
reading_goal: Understand the meaning of the LF/CRLF warnings that frequently appear in Windows.
code:
warning: in the working copy of src/pwa/app.js,
LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it
question: What is the main point of this warning?
choices: The file contents are definitely corrupted.
Line break formatting may change during the Git processing.
The remote repository has been deleted.
answer: Line break formatting may change during the Git processing.
explanation: This warning says Git's line-ending conversion settings may later turn LF in the working tree into CRLF. It usually is not an immediate failure, but it can produce whole-file diffs or tool inconsistencies. Agree on .gitattributes and core.autocrlf policy and inspect the actual diff.
project_context: This card explains the "LF to CRLF" warning that appears every time you run `git add`.

title: Defining the Commit Scope
reading_goal: I understand why we should group only related changes into a single commit.
code:
git add data/lessons/python_git_github_workflow_v33.json src/pwa/app.js
git commit -m "Add Git workflow reading cards"
question: Why does this commit scope feel natural?
choices: Because I put all the project files in there
This is because the new lesson file and the app.js file linked to it serve the same purpose.
Because we made sure to include the temporary ps1 as well
Because it was saved in the browser cache
answer: This is because the new lesson file and the app.js file linked to it serve the same purpose.
explanation: Commit scope is the criterion for determining what range of changes to group into a single commit. Grouping related changes together makes it easier to review and revert them. Mixing fixes for different features with documentation updates in a single commit can make it difficult to trace the cause of issues later on. Therefore, the correct answer is “because the new lesson file and the app.js file that links to it serve the same purpose.”
project_context: It’s best to keep the commit for adding the extension card clean by including only the connection between the lesson JSON and app.js.

title: Read the Patch Script Guide
reading_goal: I understand why the remaining patch `ps1` is not added to Git after execution.
question: Why do I check `git status` after deleting the patch script?
choices: To automatically generate the correct answers for the flashcards
To check if there are any untracked files left
answer: To check if there are any untracked files left
explanation: Delete only the exact temporary script you have verified, then use git status to find remaining untracked files or unexpected changes. -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue can hide a deletion failure, so the status check matters. If a tool is worth keeping, review it and place it in an intentional project location instead.
project_context: This has been my routine for tidying up after working on v27 through v32.

title: Read the tracking status for origin/main
reading_goal: Understand the sentence describing the relationship between local and remote branches.
code:
On branch main
Your branch is up to date with origin/main.
question: What does “up to date with origin/main” mean?
choices: Local main and the locally stored origin/main point to the same commit
GitHub's server was just queried live
answer: Local main and the locally stored origin/main point to the same commit
explanation: origin/main is a local remote-tracking ref updated by the latest successful fetch or pull. This message says local main is neither ahead of nor behind that stored ref; it does not query the server at that moment. Run a successful git fetch before comparing with the latest remote state.
project_context: This is the key line that checks whether the process exited normally after the commit and push were completed.
